mechanism_narrative: A high level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses equity valuations by increasing the discount rate applied to future cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above 5.0% or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the CPI index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% signals rising inflation, prompting expectations of aggressive monetary tightening that depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in the last month
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of months where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% over the prior month or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment (UNRATE) and declines in industrial production (INDPRO) signal an imminent economic contraction, triggering risk-off sentiment that drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE > 4.0 and INDPRO < 100 or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, strong housing starts (HOUST > 1300) indicate an overheating economy that leads to Federal Reserve tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1300 during a late-cycle expansion or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 3.5%) signals a tight labor market that fuels wage inflation and prompts aggressive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of months with UNRATE < 3.5% or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) both exceed historical thresholds, the economy overheats, triggering Fed tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS > 700000 and HOUST > 1300 or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below the 2017 base (INDPRO < 100) indicates an economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100 or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of total nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market that supports robust consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS is above 155 million or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
